description: Report personal-data shapes in structured logs, by field and class and never by value. A payment card is confirmed by the Luhn check and an account number by its own mod-97 checksum, so a match is a plausible real value rather than any digit run, which keeps an order number from being reported as a card. A date of birth needs a field named for one as well as a date. Each match reports its field, how many lines carry it and how many distinct values there are. Pay 180000 atomic USDC on Base via exact x402. MCP does not pay; it provides a challenge handoff.

allow_fields.description: Fields where a match is expected and intended. Each exclusion is recorded as something not examined rather than silently dropped.

logs.description: Newline-delimited JSON, one object per line, at most 20000 lines. A line that does not parse is reported rather than discarded. Nothing is fetched: no backend is queried and no credential is accepted, so the data supplied is the whole input.

name: pii_shape_audit

clean.description: True only when no recognised shape was found and nothing was excluded. Not a statement that the logs hold no personal data: a name, an address or a free-text note is not found here.

complete.description: Whether everything supplied was examined. False means part of it was not, which is a different problem from something that is wrong.

fields.description: Per field and class: how many lines carry it and how many distinct values. Never a value.

finding_count.description: The true total, even when the listing is bounded.

passed.description: The same verdict under the name shared across the caller-supplied families.

request_id.description: Delivery request identifier; also returned in x-foundry-request-id.

shape_classes.description: Every class looked for, published so a caller can see what was and was not covered.

title: PII Shape Audit
